summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, chronic venous insufficiency, lipodermatosclerosis, bioprosthetic aortic valve, pacemaker, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was admitted for worsening erythema, swelling, and pain in both lower extremities, despite being on suppressive cephalexin and a recent course of doxycycline. She presented with mild constitutional symptoms and a low temperature, prompting evaluation. Initial labs showed stable renal function with a mild pre-renal pattern that resolved after holding torsemide. IV vancomycin and Zosyn were started, and imaging ruled out osteomyelitis. The patient improved clinically and was transitioned to oral linezolid and ciprofloxacin for a two-week course. Stool testing for C. difficile was negative, though she experienced antibiotic-associated diarrhea. She remained stable throughout the admission, with no sepsis or decompensation of heart failure. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics, with instructions to resume her home medications, monitor weight, and follow up with infectious disease and anticoagulation clinics.
